title: The Fifth-Floor Kingdom
summary: Carrie reaches apartment 5B with the Viking household; Bjorn fixates on the small door and the key Carrie still controls while Gunnar quietly studies the building's routes.
settingText: Bushwick fifth-floor walk-up arrival sequence: stairwell landing -> hallway outside apartment 5B -> threshold at 5B. Worn but ordinary residential interior with scuffed painted walls, old linoleum, radiator pipes, apartment doors, and modest daylight; no exaggerated decay.

panelPlan.location: fifth-floor stairwell landing opening into the hallway
panelPlan.action: Carrie reaches the fifth floor first, slightly winded, carrying the thick DTI intake packet. Bjorn, Gunnar, Astrid and the two male Kin climb the last stairs behind her as one readable household group. Apartment 5B is visible farther down the narrow hallway. The building is worn, ordinary and cramped rather than threatening.

panelPlan.location: hallway directly outside apartment 5B
panelPlan.action: Carrie stops at the door marked 5B and produces the small temporary brass key. She is tired but faintly satisfied to have gotten them here. Bjorn and Gunnar have just arrived behind her; Astrid and the two male Kin remain together farther back in the hall.

panelPlan.location: hallway directly outside apartment 5B
panelPlan.action: Bjorn studies the modest apartment door, the narrow hallway around it, then Carrie. His face stays controlled and serious: he is trying to reconcile Carrie's claim that she fought for this placement with how small and unimpressive it appears.

panelPlan.location: same fifth-floor hallway, angled to include the stairwell and roof-access end
panelPlan.action: While Carrie and Bjorn remain focused on apartment 5B, Gunnar turns away from them and quietly studies the building geometry: the stairwell they used, the length of the hall, and the roof-access door at the opposite end. His attention is practical and automatic, not theatrical.

panelPlan.location: threshold of apartment 5B
panelPlan.action: Carrie inserts the brass key into the lock and begins opening the apartment herself. Bjorn's gaze drops from the door to the key in her hand and stays there as the lock turns.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Fifth floor. No elevator. I fought for the window.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: You fought for this room?

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: I fought a housing spreadsheet. It was uglier than you think.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: One stair. One hall. Two ways out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Please do not start with ways out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: A hall is judged first by its doors.

directionInline.text: The same scratched brass apartment key remains visible with Carrie; she does not surrender it yet.

title: One Very Efficient Room
summary: The three Kin enter the one-room studio together and immediately begin making it usable while Gunnar discovers the fire escape before Carrie can finish explaining the placement.
settingText: Bushwick studio apartment / Safe Cave, first entry

panelPlan.location: Door opens onto the cramped studio
panelPlan.action: Door opens onto the cramped studio: drywall, radiator, small kitchenette, old windows, sparse municipal placement furniture. The Kin stop, absorb it, then begin moving with practical purpose.

panelPlan.location: Door opens onto the cramped studio
panelPlan.action: Carrie sets the DTI packet on the tiny kitchen table and tries to establish the status of the placement.

panelPlan.location: Door opens onto the cramped studio
panelPlan.action: Bjorn stands in the center of the room, physically enormous against the low ordinary ceiling.

panelPlan.location: Door opens onto the cramped studio
panelPlan.action: Gunnar checks sink, radiator, window latches and the narrow path to the bathroom in one continuous visual scan.

panelPlan.location: Door opens onto the cramped studio
panelPlan.action: Astrid and the two male Kin remain clustered together at the main window. Astrid lifts the sash while the two men peer past her at the iron fire escape; Gunnar looks from the stairs to Carrie.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Okay. This is temporary housing. How temporary is still apparently a mystery.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: This is one room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Legally, it is one very efficient room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: Water there. Heat there. Street below. Roof above.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Yes. And the roof is not part of the apartment.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: Then why does the window have a road to it?

directionInline.text: Keep apartment geography fixed from this page onward: entry door, kitchenette/table, radiator, main window/fire escape, and sleeping area retain their relative positions.

title: Walls and Water
summary: Gunnar tests the pipes and hot-water tap; the household stops at the discovery of reliable hot water while Bjorn asks who controls it.
settingText: Bushwick studio kitchenette and bathroom threshold

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio kitchenette and bathroom threshold
panelPlan.action: Gunnar kneels by the exposed radiator pipe while Astrid and the two male Kin remain together at the kitchenette; Astrid tests the sink tap as the two men watch the water and Gunnar follows the pipe into the wall.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio kitchenette and bathroom threshold
panelPlan.action: Clear water runs from the faucet over Gunnar's callused hand.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio kitchenette and bathroom threshold
panelPlan.action: Bjorn looks from the running tap to Carrie and asks who commands the water. Carrie leans against the counter and answers him literally, without smiling at the question.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio kitchenette and bathroom threshold
panelPlan.action: Steam gathers faintly as Gunnar discovers the hot-water side. His reaction is quiet, sincere and impressed.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio kitchenette beside the sink and radiator
panelPlan.action: For a beat the room is still: ancient travelers listening to pipes inside a wall. Carrie leans against the counter, letting the moment be real.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: The wall carries water.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: The pipe carries water.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: Who commands it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Nobody in this room. The city sends it; the building keeps the pipes working.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: Hot.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Yes. Hot water. Every day, when the building behaves.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: Your city wastes miracles casually.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Give it a week.

directionInline.text: Use tactile ordinary apartment plumbing and heat: old fixtures, chipped sink enamel, painted radiator surfaces, and visible steam where appropriate.

title: The Packet Comes Home
summary: Carrie opens the placement packet; Bjorn refuses to mark unread terms, forcing Carrie to stop treating the paperwork as a formality and negotiate the agreement with him.
settingText: Bushwick studio kitchen table

panelPlan.location: Kitchen table becomes a tiny negotiation table
panelPlan.action: The tiny kitchen table is crowded with Carrie's thick DTI packet, temporary badge, cheap pen and the brass key still in her hand. Bjorn sits opposite her; Gunnar and the three Kin remain close enough to follow the exchange.

panelPlan.location: Kitchen table becomes a tiny negotiation table
panelPlan.action: Carrie sits and squares the packet toward Bjorn.

panelPlan.location: Kitchen table becomes a tiny negotiation table
panelPlan.action: Bjorn remains standing; Carrie answers the implied accusation instead of ordering him to sit.

panelPlan.location: Kitchen table becomes a tiny negotiation table
panelPlan.action: His finger rests beside dense municipal print but never pretends he can read it.

panelPlan.location: Kitchen table becomes a tiny negotiation table
panelPlan.action: Bjorn states the actual problem. Carrie closes her laptop/phone and gives the paper her full attention.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Before anyone claims the roof, the hallway, the water, or New Jersey, we need the intake finished.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: Finished? We sat beneath the white lights for half a day.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: That was intake. This is placement.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: The same oath with a different name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Different form. Same soul damage.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: I will not bind my people to words I cannot judge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Then we judge them. One clause at a time.

title: Terms of the Hall
summary: Carrie reads out the apartment restrictions; Bjorn and Gunnar test each rule against the room, ending with Gunnar focused on the fire escape.
settingText: Bushwick studio kitchen table with fire-escape window visible

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio kitchen table with fire-escape window visible
panelPlan.action: Packet open with highlighted housing clauses. Brass key beside it; the fire escape is visible through the background window.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio kitchen table with fire-escape window visible
panelPlan.action: Carrie counts the important rules on her fingers instead of reading legal boilerplate.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio kitchen table with fire-escape window visible
panelPlan.action: Bjorn notices that the rules describe the same categories any hall must regulate.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio kitchen table with fire-escape window visible
panelPlan.action: Gunnar points to the fire escape; Carrie answers before he can build a theory.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio kitchen table with fire-escape window visible
panelPlan.action: Bjorn gives Carrie the first trace of respect for having foreseen obvious sources of conflict.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: No open flame outside the stove. No cutting into walls. No livestock. No hunting on shared property.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: The rules concern fire, walls, animals, and territory.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Most housing law eventually does.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: What of the iron stair outside the window?

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Emergency exit. Not a porch. Not a watchtower. Not additional square footage.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: You have anticipated us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: I have met people before.

title: What the Window Is For
summary: Gunnar and Bjorn test the fire escape and rig a pigeon snare while Astrid and the two male Kin remain together inside the apartment window, helping from the sill; Carrie notices the rope from inside.
settingText: Bushwick fire escape and adjacent rooftop edge

panelPlan.location: studio interior at the open main window, looking onto the fire escape
panelPlan.action: From inside the studio, the open main window frames the old iron fire escape, neighboring brick walls, tar roofs, water towers and ordinary Bushwick skyline. Gunnar is already outside; Astrid and the two male Kin remain together just inside the window.

panelPlan.location: fire escape immediately outside the studio window; three Kin remain inside at the sill
panelPlan.action: Gunnar tests the fire-escape railing and stair load. At the open window, Astrid and the two male Kin stay together; one of the men feeds rope through the opening while Astrid and the other man hold the coil inside.

panelPlan.location: studio window and fire escape with neighboring parapet visible
panelPlan.action: Pigeons cluster on the neighboring parapet. Gunnar works the small improvised loop outside while Astrid and the two male Kin watch together from the apartment window; one of them points out the birds.

panelPlan.location: fire escape immediately outside the studio window
panelPlan.action: Bjorn joins Gunnar on the fire escape and both crouch behind the parapet with complete hunting seriousness. The three Kin remain visible together through the open apartment window behind them.

panelPlan.location: studio window / fire-escape threshold
panelPlan.action: Carrie reaches the apartment window from inside and follows the rope line out to Gunnar and Bjorn. Astrid and the two male Kin stand together beside her at the sill. Gunnar answers without turning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: The iron stair holds three men. Four if the small one does not move.

dialogueInline.speaker: The Kin
dialogueInline.text: Birds gather on the next roof.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: Fat birds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: They do not fear us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: They have not needed to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Gunnar? Why is there rope going out my window?

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: It is not your window now.

title: The Bird Is Evidence
summary: The pigeon snare catches one bird; Silas films from outside while Carrie makes Gunnar and Bjorn release it and clear the fire escape.
settingText: Bushwick fire escape, apartment window, and neighboring exterior sightline

panelPlan.location: Bushwick fire escape, apartment window, and neighboring exterior sightline
panelPlan.action: The improvised loop has caught one ordinary city pigeon without gore or injury. Gunnar steadies the bird on the fire escape while Astrid and the two male Kin remain together just inside the open window, watching; Bjorn studies the catch as possible food.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick fire escape, apartment window, and neighboring exterior sightline
panelPlan.action: Across the narrow exterior gap, Silas has his phone up, documenting rope, bread, bird and the occupied fire escape.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick fire escape, apartment window, and neighboring exterior sightline
panelPlan.action: Carrie leans through the apartment window, sees both the bird and Silas's phone, and understands the practical problem instantly.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick fire escape, apartment window, and neighboring exterior sightline
panelPlan.action: Bjorn looks from Carrie to Silas. Carrie is firm but not humiliating him; this is a boundary with a reason.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick fire escape, apartment window, and neighboring exterior sightline
panelPlan.action: Gunnar releases the pigeon. It beats away over the rooftops while the Kin pull the rope back inside and Silas lowers his phone a little.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: Caught.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: Small. But fat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Silas
dialogueInline.text: Please tell me that is not dinner.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Release the bird.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: It entered our snare.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: You forbade hunting on shared ground. This is outside our window.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: And directly outside everybody else's windows. That is what shared means.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: Shared boundary. Understood.

directionInline.text: The pigeon remains ordinary and unharmed.

title: Treaty Presentation

settingText: Bushwick studio apartment kitchen table

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio apartment kitchen table
panelPlan.action: The rope and bread are back inside. Carrie clears a corner of the cramped table and lays the DTI placement packet flat beside a cheap ballpoint pen.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio apartment kitchen table
panelPlan.action: Carrie's finger lands on the acknowledgement line and signature box.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio apartment kitchen table
panelPlan.action: Bjorn does not take the pen. He looks at Carrie, not the paper.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio apartment kitchen table
panelPlan.action: Carrie starts to answer procedurally, then stops because his distinction is accurate.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio apartment kitchen table
panelPlan.action: Bjorn taps the translated clauses they discussed earlier, separating agreement from unread authorship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Okay. Bird released. Exterior empire postponed. Back to placement.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: DTI needs the acknowledgement executed before they close this out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: We judged the terms.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: Then why must I make your mark beneath words I cannot read?

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Because the system needs proof you agreed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: Proof of agreement is not proof that I wrote this.

title: The Mark and the Meaning
summary: Carrie tries the obvious modern workaround—signing by copying a name—but Bjorn rejects imitation as false witness. Gunnar, watching the packet like a piece of equipment, asks what DTI actually requires the mark to prove.
settingText: Bushwick studio apartment kitchen table

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio apartment kitchen table
panelPlan.action: Carrie writes BJORN clearly on scrap paper beside the form, demonstrating rather than patronizing.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio apartment kitchen table
panelPlan.action: She offers the pen. Bjorn studies the copied letters, then leaves the pen on the table.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio apartment kitchen table
panelPlan.action: Bjorn points to Carrie's handwriting and then to himself: the objection is authorship, not fear of the tool.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio apartment kitchen table
panelPlan.action: Gunnar rotates the form ninety degrees on the table and traces the printed boxes, labels and signature line with one finger.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio apartment kitchen table
panelPlan.action: Carrie looks at the form again. Her frustration shifts away from Bjorn and toward the procedure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: You could copy your name. Right here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: Those are your strokes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: They would become yours if you made them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: Then I would swear I know what I do not know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: What does the box require: his name, or his agreement?

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: It says signature.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: That was not my question.

dialogueInline.text: Heat needs air around it.

dialogueInline.text: Move mine too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Carrie.
